Enforcing workspace manifold filters at the proposal boundary prevents trajectory optimizers from driving actuators into kinematic lockup.

A target inside the static workspace\index{Kinematics!workspace} may still be out of reach within the time its evidence stays valid. **Dynamic reachability**\index{Dynamic reachability} is the condition that the end effector can move from its measured state $(\mathbf{p}_0, \mathbf{v}_0)$ to the target pose within the remaining window $t_{\text{exp}} - t_{\text{now}}$ while respecting its velocity, acceleration, jerk, and thermal torque limits. Whatever profile the actuators follow, no move covers a distance $d$ faster than its speed ceiling allows, so admission requires at least
$$\frac{d}{v_{\max}} \le t_{\text{exp}} - t_{\text{now}}.$$ {#eq-intent-dynamic-reachability-bound}
Acceleration and jerk limits only lengthen the transit, so a proposal that fails this inequality fails every fuller test. If a motion controller attempts to execute a trajectory toward a target that violates @eq-intent-dynamic-reachability-bound, the solver either demands infinite acceleration or the controller saturates actuator velocity limits, inducing severe phase lag, drive bus overcurrent trips, or an emergency stop midway through transit. @Sec-appendix-control-reachability derives the triangular, trapezoidal, and jerk-limited profiles those limits produce.

Evaluating this kinematic lower bound (@eq-intent-dynamic-reachability-bound) acts as a **zero-cost algorithmic gatekeeper**\index{Zero-cost algorithmic gatekeeper!definition}. Non-linear trajectory optimizers (such as TrajOpt or sequential quadratic programming) consume $50\text{--}200\text{ ms}$ of CPU time searching for dynamically feasible paths. Passing a target that physically cannot be reached within the remaining lease window forces the optimizer to search an empty solution set until it exhausts its iteration limit, starving the real-time scheduler. The dynamic transit check rejects impossible proposals in under a microsecond before invoking computationally intensive solvers.

On the arm, the mug's evidence under the qualified tracker stays valid for `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str`, and at the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.v_tcp_str` tool center point (TCP) speed limit the gripper covers at most `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.d_reach_tracked_str` in that window. A proposal issued with the gripper `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.d_target_str` from the handle needs at least `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_transit_floor_str` of transit, so the MCU rejects it with `ERR_DYNAMIC_TIME_INSUFFICIENT` before any path is solved. Without the tracker the window shrinks to `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str` and the reach to `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.d_reach_untracked_str`, so an untracked reach can close only the last few centimeters of an approach. Passing the inequality only permits the fuller path, torque, and stopping check.

The physical interaction between target-evidence validity and dynamic transit time floors governs whether an intent lease can be admitted into execution (@fig-10-intent-lease-horizon). When target drift is high or tracking is lost (panel a), evidence validity decays along hyperbolic bounds, collapsing below deliberative VLA inference latency and demanding local high-rate trackers. In turn, actuator velocity and acceleration ceilings impose a strict transit time floor $t_{\text{transit}}$ (panel b): if the commanded motion distance exceeds the dynamic reach of the remaining lease window $\tau_{\text{lease}}$, the admission layer rejects the proposal immediately without allocating motion planning compute.

::: {#fig-10-intent-lease-horizon fig-env="figure" fig-pos="htb" fig-cap="**Target-Evidence Horizon and Dynamic Reachability Filter**: Quantitative bounds governing grounded intent admission under target drift and plant dynamics. Panel (a) evaluates the target-evidence validity horizon $\tau_{\text{ev}} \le (r_{\text{tol}} - e_0) / v_{\text{drift}}$ across precision insertion ($r_{\text{tol}} = 8\,\text{mm}$), standard grasp ($15\,\text{mm}$), and coarse pick ($30\,\text{mm}$) tolerances with initial measurement error $e_0 = 3\,\text{mm}$. When drift velocity exceeds $100\,\text{mm/s}$, evidence validity collapses below the 180 ms nominal edge VLA inference horizon, rendering upstream proposals stale before execution begins unless refreshed by a 50 Hz local tracker. Panel (b) evaluates the dynamic reachability filter comparing minimum transit time $t_{\text{transit}}$ against the remaining lease window $\tau_{\text{lease}}$. A 150 ms untracked lease admits only short terminal adjustments ($d \le 11\,\text{mm}$), triggering immediate rejection (`ERR_DYNAMIC_TIME_INSUFFICIENT`) for distant goals before path planning begins." fig-alt="Two-panel quantitative analysis of intent lease admission. Panel (a) plots target-evidence horizon in milliseconds against target physical drift velocity from 5 to 350 millimeters per second, showing hyperbolic decay curves across three grasp tolerances and highlighting the stale evidence hazard zone relative to 650 millisecond VLA tail latency and 20 millisecond local tracker loops. Panel (b) plots minimum transit time in milliseconds against required tool-center-point travel distance from 10 to 450 millimeters, showing trapezoidal acceleration curves intersecting 150 millisecond untracked and 450 millisecond tracked lease horizons with shaded inadmissible regions."}
![](images/png/fig10_intent_lease_horizon.png){width="100%"}
:::

This bound and the fuller checks behind it rest on imported rigid-body mechanics under three assumptions, namely that actuator torque-speed curves remain within nominal thermal ratings, joint encoders accurately report the initial state $(\mathbf{p}_0, \mathbf{v}_0)$, and the payload mass matches the inertial model behind the actuator limits. A representative permission-path implementation monitors joint current\index{Joint current}, motor temperature\index{Joule heating}, and communication delay\index{Bus latency} at rates chosen from the plant and sensor budgets. These observations can detect some departures from the model but cannot verify every assumption, such as payload inertia, on every tick.

If motor winding temperatures exceed the thermal thresholds of @sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles, the permission path imposes thermal derating\index{Thermal derating}, scaling down the maximum allowed acceleration ($a_{\max}$) and velocity ($v_{\max}$) in the parameter registry. An external force measurement that indicates a payload mass deviation lowers the same limits. The intent filter immediately evaluates subsequent incoming leases against these reduced physical limits. A derating event can make a previously admitted path infeasible; the controller must recheck it and select a feasible fallback if the margin is lost.

When the reachability filter rejects an intent proposal, it must not simply discard the packet. Discarding without feedback leaves the upstream reasoning model unaware of why motion failed to occur, forcing it to wait for an end-to-end task timeout. The intent filter generates an immediate, structured diagnostic packet returned directly to the reasoning layer across the proposal boundary. This diagnostic payload contains the rejection classification, such as a kinematic workspace violation (`ERR_WORKSPACE_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`), dynamic time insufficiency (`ERR_DYNAMIC_TIME_INSUFFICIENT`), or swept-volume collision intersection (`ERR_OCCUPANCY_BLOCKED`), along with the numerical margins of failure. For a dynamic reachability failure, the feedback returns the shortfall between the transit lower bound and the remaining window, and the maximum reachable distance along the commanded vector within the allotted lease. For a static workspace violation, the feedback provides the projection of the target onto the boundary of $\mathcal{W}$ (the closest physical point the arm can actually reach). The reasoning layer uses this structured signal to adjust its proposal on the subsequent inference cycle, by obtaining fresher evidence, choosing an alternate approach, slowing or pausing the process, or proposing base relocation. It cannot extend the evidence horizon without a new justification.

Reachability filters remove targets the body cannot reach, or cannot reach in time, and leave the complete motion to the planner and the permission path.

### Dynamic obstacle forecasting and reachable exclusion zones {#sec-intent-dynamic-forecasting}

Kinematic workspace and dynamic transit bounds evaluate whether the machine's own body can attain the commanded pose within the evidence window. However, physical AI agents rarely operate in isolation; they share physical workspaces with moving human coworkers, automated guided vehicles, and other mobile manipulators. Grounding intent in a shared environment requires extending the admission filter from static obstacle occupancy to **dynamic obstacle forecasting**\index{Dynamic obstacle!reachability forecasting}\index{Dynamic reachability!exclusion cones}.

Consuming the dynamic track manifest $[(\text{ID}_k, \hat{\mathbf{p}}_k, \hat{\mathbf{v}}_k, \mathbf{P}_k, t_{\text{last}}, \text{state})]$ published by the multi-object tracker (@sec-perception-tracking-association), the intent filter must not treat tracked obstacles as static bounding spheres. As an obstacle moves, its future position is a time-varying spatial volume that expands forward in time. For each confirmed or coasting track $k$, the admission engine constructs the **dynamic reachability cone** $\mathcal{R}_k(\tau)$ of @eq-intent-reachability-cone over the candidate execution horizon $\tau \in [0, T_{\text{horizon}}]$:
$$\mathcal{R}_k(\tau) = \left\{ \mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3 \;\middle|\; \|\mathbf{p} - (\hat{\mathbf{p}}_k + \hat{\mathbf{v}}_k \tau)\| \le r_k + \frac{1}{2} a_{k,\max} \tau^2 + k_\sigma \sigma_{\text{track}}(\tau) \right\}$$ {#eq-intent-reachability-cone}
where:

- $r_k$ is the conservative bounding radius of the tracked entity (e.g., $r_k = 0.35\text{ m}$ enclosing a human coworker's torso and shoulders).
- $\frac{1}{2} a_{k,\max} \tau^2$ models worst-case kinematic expansion under unobserved acceleration, where $a_{k,\max}$ is the actor's physical acceleration limit (e.g., $a_{\max} \approx 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$ for agile pedestrian maneuvers).
- $k_\sigma$ is the statistical confidence multiplier (e.g., $k_\sigma = 3$, corresponding to the 99.7 percent three-sigma Gaussian confidence boundary).
- $\mathbf{H} = [\mathbf{I}_{3\times3} \mid \mathbf{0}_{3\times3}]$ is the linear state projection matrix that maps the six-dimensional kinematic state vector $[\mathbf{p}^\top, \mathbf{v}^\top]^\top$ down to 3D Cartesian coordinates.
- $\sigma_{\text{track}}(\tau) = \sqrt{\text{tr}(\mathbf{H}\mathbf{P}_{t+\tau}\mathbf{H}^\top)}$ captures the root-mean-square spatial tracking standard deviation $\sqrt{\sigma_x^2 + \sigma_y^2 + \sigma_z^2}$, growing monotonically under unobserved process noise during sensor dropouts or coasting intervals.

As illustrated in @fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones, the intent filter evaluates candidate robot transit corridors $\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(\tau)$ against each obstacle's reachability cone. An intent proposal is admitted only if the swept spatial volume of the machine guarantees non-intersection across the entire proposed execution window:
$$\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(\tau) \cap \mathcal{R}_k(\tau) = \emptyset \quad \forall \tau \in [0, T_{\text{lease}}], \;\; \forall k$$ {#eq-intent-dynamic-exclusion}
If the candidate path intersects an expanding cone (as shown in panel a, where the nominal candidate trajectory intersects $\mathcal{R}(t_2)$ of the walking coworker), the admission gate immediately evaluates @eq-intent-dynamic-exclusion and refuses the proposal with `ERR_DYNAMIC_OCCUPANCY_CONFLICT`. Admitting an intersecting intent lease would force the downstream tracking controller into an emergency braking maneuver or safe stop midway through execution, causing task oscillation and unnecessary wear. The refusal diagnostic returns the earliest predicted conflict time $\tau_{\text{conflict}}$ and the conflicting actor identifier $\text{ID}_k$ to the upstream reasoning layer, directing the model to select an alternate corridor or yield until the dynamic exclusion zone clears.

A subtle yet critical hazard of quadratic forward reachability sets ($\frac{1}{2} a_{\max} \tau^2$) is the notorious **freezing robot problem**\index{Freezing robot problem!mitigation via short leases}. If an autonomous mobile robot projects human pedestrian reachability over a multi-second planning horizon ($\tau = 2.0\text{ s}$) with an agile sprint acceleration capability ($a_{\max} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$), the exclusion cone radius expands by $4.0\text{ meters}$. In an active industrial warehouse or crowded hospital corridor, these massive forward reachability cones overlap, instantly consuming all free space and forcing the robot to freeze indefinitely. Practical physical AI systems defeat this paralysis through three architectural countermeasures:

1. *Short Intent Lease Horizons:* By restricting intent leases to short, receding temporal horizons ($\tau \le 200\text{--}400\text{ ms}$), the quadratic expansion term remains tightly contained ($\frac{1}{2} a_{\max} \tau^2 \le 0.04\text{--}0.16\text{ m}$), preserving navigable corridors.
2. *Velocity Capping:* Physical human pedestrians cannot accelerate indefinitely; their reachable sets are clipped by an absolute maximum velocity cap ($v_{\max} \approx 1.6\text{ m/s}$), transforming parabolic cones into linear cylinders for longer horizons.
3. *High-Rate Recursive Re-centering:* Local trackers running at $50\text{ Hz}$ continuously re-center the cone origin on fresh sensor measurements ($t_0 \leftarrow t_{\text{fresh}}$) and collapse tracking covariance, preventing the cumulative uncertainty explosion that causes trajectory starvation.

::: {#fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Dynamic reachability cones and multi-object tracking lifecycle**: (a) Top-down bird's-eye view (BEV) of a shared workspace. A moving coworker (track 42) generates forward-expanding reachability cones $\\mathcal{R}(t)$ whose radii grow quadratically with the actor's acceleration capability $a_{\\max}$ and tracking covariance $\\sigma_{\\text{track}}$. When a proposed robot trajectory intersects $\\mathcal{R}(t_2)$, the intent gate rejects the lease with `ERR_DYNAMIC_OCCUPANCY`, admitting only verified detour or yield profiles. (b) Multi-object tracking state lifecycle, transitioning candidate detections through a chi-squared Mahalanobis validation gate and Hungarian bipartite matching into tentative, confirmed, coasting (with covariance inflation $\\mathbf{P}_{t+1} = \\mathbf{F}\\mathbf{P}\\mathbf{F}^\\top + \\mathbf{Q}$), and terminated states." fig-alt="Two-panel systems diagram. Left panel shows top-down warehouse layout with a robot planning a path toward a goal, a walking coworker with three expanding circular reachability cones R(t1), R(t2), R(t3), and a red conflict crosshatch where the path intersects R(t2) triggering an intent refusal gate. Right panel shows a state machine for multi-object tracking from sensor ingress to validation gate, Hungarian match, tentative, confirmed, coasting, and terminated states, outputting a dynamic track manifest schema."}
![](images/svg/fig10_dynamic_reachability_cones.svg){width="100%"}
:::

In @fig-10-dynamic-reachability-cones, the two panels illustrate the physical mechanics and software tracking state machine that underpin dynamic safety:

- *Panel (a): Bird's-Eye View (BEV) Dynamic Reachability Conflict:* The warehouse floor plan shows a mobile manipulator evaluating a transit trajectory $\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(\tau)$ through an intersection. A moving coworker (tracked entity 42) walks toward the aisle crossing. The admission engine projects forward three expanding reachability cones $\mathcal{R}(t_1), \mathcal{R}(t_2), \mathcal{R}(t_3)$, whose radii grow quadratically with the coworker's acceleration capability ($\frac{1}{2}a_{\max}\tau^2$) and linearly with tracking covariance ($k_\sigma\sigma_{\text{track}}$). At future epoch $t_2$, the candidate robot corridor intersects $\mathcal{R}(t_2)$ (highlighted by the red crosshatched collision zone). Rather than launching the robot and forcing an emergency stop midway through, the intent admission engine evaluates $\mathcal{T}_{\text{robot}}(t_2) \cap \mathcal{R}_{42}(t_2) \neq \emptyset$, instantly rejecting the lease with `ERR_DYNAMIC_OCCUPANCY_CONFLICT` and directing the planner to formulate an evasive detour or yield.
- *Panel (b): Multi-object tracking state lifecycle:* The software state machine coordinates target persistence through occlusion:
  1. *Measurement Ingress & Gating:* Sensor returns enter a chi-squared Mahalanobis distance validation gate ($d_M \le \gamma$) to filter spurious noise.
  2. *Bipartite Matching:* A Hungarian assignment algorithm matches gated detections to existing active tracks.
  3. *State Progression:*
     - *Tentative:* New unconfirmed returns must be detected across $N_{\text{init}}$ consecutive frames before motion authority is granted.
     - *Confirmed:* Actively observed entities receive recursive Kalman measurement updates, keeping spatial covariance bounded.
     - *Coasting:* When an obstacle passes behind a shelf or enters an occlusion zone, measurement updates cease. The tracker preserves track identity, propagating the state purely via the kinematic transition matrix ($\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{t+1} = \mathbf{F}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_t$) while inflating covariance on every tick ($\mathbf{P}_{t+1} = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{P}_t\mathbf{F}^\top + \mathbf{Q}$).
     - *Terminated:* If covariance expands beyond safety margins or occlusion persists beyond a timeout horizon, the track is evicted from the active manifest.

Reachability filters and dynamic exclusion zones together eliminate targets and corridors that the physical machine cannot safely execute, passing only spatially and temporally admissible candidates to the trajectory optimizer and safety enforcer.

## Intent Grounding Failure Modes and Affordance Invalidation {#sec-intent-failure-modes}

When a vision-language model\index{Vision-language model} outputs an $SE(3)$ target pose\index{SE(3) Kinematics} for a physical manipulator, that pose can fail in several distinct ways. It may be a hallucinated target generated from visual attention patterns on reflective background textures. It may be a stale target representing an object that a human coworker bumped or displaced moments earlier while the camera pipeline was buffering frames. It may be a reference ambiguity where the model arbitrarily selects one of two identical red mugs side by side on the conveyor without resolving which one the task requires. Or it may stem from an out-of-distribution scene shift, such as unexpected lighting or dust on an optical lens, that degrades the spatial prediction accuracy of the network. Despite their different causes, these failures arrive downstream in the same form.

The planner receives a dated target proposal, not an actuator command. A pose on an empty location may lead to a futile reach; a pose inside an occupied fixture may lead to contact if the later path and permission checks fail. In the wrong-object case, by contrast, the geometry can be valid while the selected object is semantically wrong. The independent permission path therefore checks what it can measure (freshness, coverage, geometry, current state, and actuator limits) without claiming to verify the task's meaning. **The Safety MCU enforces physical feasibility, not semantic truth: a goal can be perfectly collision-free, kinematically smooth, and torque-limited, yet completely wrong for the task.** If a vision-language model confuses an expensive camera lens with a compliant rubber ball, the downstream controller will execute a smooth, authorized grasp that fractures the lens. Semantic verification belongs to upstream task monitoring and operator oversight; the physical permission path guarantees only that execution does not violate conservation laws or plant safety envelopes.

A fresh depth observation can reject a proposed grasp whose required object evidence is absent in a covered, visible region. No return in an occluded or unobserved region leaves the region unknown. A task-specific ambiguity test runs on every proposal, confident or not, because a high score describes the model's certainty and cannot show that no second candidate shares the pick window. The test refuses a window that holds two candidates, and the item goes to the coworker for a manual pick. The permission path runs it on its side of the proposal boundary, as the ambiguity gate of @fig-10-lease-dynamics-tradeoff (panel b), on evidence the grounding model does not produce; the producer's entropy filter can refuse earlier but cannot replace it.

@Tbl-10-grounding-failure-modes groups these failures by the check that catches them, adds two that the model's output cannot reveal until contact or timing exposes them (a misclassified affordance and a target unreachable within its window), and separates admission checks from responses after motion or contact has begun. At the cage-door latch of \ref{nbk-intent-lease-duration-collision-exposure-tradeoff-across}, the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_contact_str` contact-loop response already leaves `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_at_brake_onset_n_str` at brake-command onset, and the peak comes later, so precontact speed and force limits, actuator response, compliance, and available clearance determine whether the full contact trace stays within the validated contact limits.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}

| Failure mode                                                             | Evidence or check                                                                                                              | Admission or response                                                                                          | Physical limit to verify                                                                                                            |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Phantom target:** image artifact in empty space                        | Fresh depth evidence and target-region occupancy, with coverage and occlusion checked                                          | Reject the proposal when the required object evidence is absent; request another view if the region is unknown | Rejection precedes motion only if the proposal has not already been admitted. Missing returns alone do not prove empty space.       |
| **Stale target:** workpiece moved after capture                          | Converted capture time, bounded clock error, local tracking, and target-error envelope                                         | Revoke dependent tracking when the evidence limit fails; select the validated fallback                         | Total detection, communication, actuation, and braking delay must fit the measured clearance.                                       |
| **Semantic ambiguity:** two candidate objects in the pick window         | Independent count of candidates in the pick window from fresh depth evidence; model entropy as an earlier producer-side signal | Refuse admission and route the item to the coworker for a manual pick                                          | A single wrong object passes the count, and a confident model can report low entropy; independent physical checks remain necessary. |
| **Misclassified affordance:** bolted fixture selected as graspable       | Contact-force and motion residuals after contact; precontact task/geometry checks where possible                               | Limit precontact speed and force, then invoke the validated contact response on a threshold crossing           | A reactive trip does not cap the first impact peak; test the full force trace, response delay, and stopping energy.                 |
| **Dynamic unreachability:** target cannot be reached in its valid window | Speed-ceiling transit lower bound followed by a complete path and stopping check                                               | Reject a proposal whose lower bound exceeds the remaining evidence window                                      | Passing the lower bound proves neither collision-free motion nor a feasible stop.                                                   |

: **Grounding failure modes and their evidence limits**: Each check addresses a different failure class. The table separates proposal rejection from a response to an already moving plant. {#tbl-10-grounding-failure-modes tbl-colwidths="[19,27,25,29]"}

Every row of the table therefore requires the proposal to carry its spatial bounds, the provenance of its evidence, and its expiry, in a form the permission path can check without the model. A rejected proposal returns a reason to the learned layer; an admitted proposal remains subject to independent permission checks as the plant moves. The proposal carries those fields across the proposal boundary, and the record the permission path grants from it is the intent lease.

## The Intent Lease Specification and Contract {#sec-intent-lease}

The intent lease takes its lineage from memory. Its parent is the belief record of @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema, named by digest, and that record's evidence epoch, converted to the MCU's clock, becomes the lease's evidence time. The lease itself carries a goal region, an error envelope and task tolerance, a requested wrench, a requested terminal mode, an evidence horizon, and an expiry. It is a lease in the sense of @sec-nervous-cadences, here on a target, and the proposal that requests it travels under the proposal header with an intent payload in place of a chunk. An admitted intent grants a target and effort ceilings, never a path.

In the machine stack's 14-record contract lineage, this stage emits the **Intent Specification** (Contract 9). While the uncertified Application Processor proposes an untrusted candidate intent proposal (@tbl-10-intent-proposal-fields) across the proposal boundary (@sec-intent-four-stage-pipeline), the Safety MCU independently evaluates and latches the admitted **Intent Specification** record (realized at runtime as the active **Intent Lease**). This cyber-physical contract binds high-level semantic intent to verified geometric goal sets, affordance frame transforms, and certified motion predicates, constraining the downstream trajectory planner (@sec-planning-behavior-seam) before any motion is admitted.

An intuitive way to conceptualize an intent lease is as a temporary parking permit. When high-level autonomy requests permission to reach toward an object or traverse an aisle, that authorization cannot be an open-ended blank check. While the robot moves, physical reality changes: an obstacle shifts, a human enters the corridor, or sensor confidence degrades. The intent lease grants bounded tracking authority only for a strictly limited duration. When the timer expires, the robot cannot coast on optimistic assumptions; it must either produce a renewed lease backed by fresh physical evidence or immediately transition to a pre-validated safe stop.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ **Byte layout:** The intent payload's fields, types, and offsets are given in @sec-appendix-systems-wire-intent.
:::

On the running machine the proposal travels from the application processor to the MCU as a fixed-size, statically parsed message in a bounded shared mailbox,[^fn-intent-intercore-channel] so its parse time can be measured against the control deadline. The message only transports a request; the independent permission controller owns the configured force ceilings, deadline ceilings, and state-dependent fallback.

[^fn-intent-intercore-channel]: **Inter-core communication across the proposal boundary**\index{Inter-core communication!RPMSG}\index{Proposal boundary!inter-core communication}: RPMSG over a statically bounded shared SRAM ring is one transport. Copy count, cache maintenance, coherency, and worst-case handoff time depend on the system-on-chip (SoC) and driver, and the MCU's independent timer detects lost renewals even through a host kernel panic. See @sec-appendix-systems-ipc.

The covariance ellipsoid of the mug-handle estimate in @sec-intent-request-to-proposal is a producer-side localization estimate. The proposal does not try to encode a general oriented $3\times3$ covariance; its bounds carry three conservative **position-error envelopes** $(e_x,e_y,e_z)$ and three requested **task tolerances** $(r_x,r_y,r_z)$ in the named robot-base frame instead. Envelope and tolerance keep the distinction drawn in @sec-intent-handoff, so admission requires $0\le e_i\le r_i$ on each axis. The producer must justify any conversion from covariance to an envelope, including calibration bias and declared tail risk. Orientation tolerances and contact-mode rules come from an independently approved task profile; the proposal carries only the target orientation itself.

The proposal's evidence time is the **belief record's evidence epoch**, never its estimate epoch, converted to the MCU's clock under the clock rule of @sec-nervous-cadences. The MCU matches both the parent digest and that epoch to a retained belief record and adds the mapping's error bound to its age test. The requested expiry uses the same clock, so the MCU can compare it directly with the evidence and stopping deadlines that bound it. The parent digest is **lineage, not message authentication**, under the integrity policy of @sec-nervous-cadences. It does not prove who chose the target, limits, or requested terminal mode, and the intent proposal carries no keyed tag because the permission path admits it by content, not origin.

The admitted intent moves through Pending, Active, Renewed, Expired, and Aborted states. The MCU enters Active only after checking the request against independently configured ceilings and a feasible response from the measured state. A renewal needs a newer sequence, a fresh belief record, and a new permission check; it does not automatically extend authority. Meeting the approved task tolerance completes the goal. Unexpected contact or loss of a required belief aborts the dependent motion.

::: {#dfn-intent-expiring-intent-lease .callout-definition title="Expiring intent lease"}

***Expiring intent lease***\index{Expiring intent lease!definition}\index{Intent lease!definition} ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) is a time-bounded execution authorization issued by the independent permission path that binds an admitted target pose and effort ceilings to a monotonic hardware deadline $t_{\text{exp}}$:
$$t_{\text{exp}} = \min(t_{\text{evidence}} + \tau_{\text{ev}}, \; t_{\text{issue}} + \tau_{\text{lease}}, \; t_{\text{stop\_deadline}})$$ {#eq-intent-lease-expiry-bound}
upon whose expiration motion tracking authority is automatically revoked without requiring an explicit cancellation packet.

1.  **Significance**: Withdraws tracking authority on a hardware deadline when upstream deliberation stalls, so the validated fallback starts without waiting for the proposer.
2.  **Distinction**: Unlike a network keepalive or software ping, an intent lease couples the horizon of physical sensor evidence ($\tau_{\text{ev}}$) with dynamic braking feasibility, and its expiry falls no later than the stop deadline at which a validated fallback still fits the remaining clearance.
3.  **Common pitfall**: Sizing lease durations generously to mask tail latency ($P_{99}$) in neural inference, which creates an unmonitored open-loop window where the robot moves through an environment that may have changed.

:::

The three terms in the minimization enforce fundamentally distinct safety bounds:

- $t_{\text{evidence}} + \tau_{\text{ev}}$ is the *physical target validity horizon*: the instant when unobserved target drift or perturbation exceeds task tolerance $r_{\text{tol}}$.
- $t_{\text{issue}} + \tau_{\text{lease}}$ is the *software administrative lease*: an upper bound on how long the deliberative application processor is permitted to remain silent before the safety MCU presumes a host deadlock or transport failure.
- $t_{\text{stop\_deadline}}$ is the *immutable physical stopping boundary*: the absolute deadline by which the robot must begin braking to ensure that physical stopping distance ($d_{\text{stop}} = v \tau_{\text{delay}} + \frac{v^2}{2a_{\text{brake}}}$) does not violate obstacle clearance.

At expiration, the timer revokes tracking authority and the MCU starts whichever of its approved hold, controlled-deceleration, and torque-disable responses the rule of @sec-intent-goals-expire selects for the measured load and contact mode. The requested terminal mode is advisory, so a request for torque disable over a suspended payload cannot override the powered hold that such a load requires. Neither a `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_permission_str` check period nor a hardware interrupt establishes a physical stop within one period.

The proposal's fields support layered checks, cheapest first, and one implementation orders them in this bounded admission sequence:

1. **Evidence and sequence:** Read a complete proposal packet. Reject an old sequence or a parent digest and evidence epoch that do not match a retained belief record. Compute evidence age in the MCU monotonic domain and add the bounded clock-conversion error. Reject when that age exceeds the target-evidence horizon.
2. **Proposal limits:** Check finite pose values, quaternion normalization, base-frame error and task-tolerance axes, and requested wrench against approved task and actuator limits. Check known occupancy and unknown-space policy.
3. **Dynamic admission:** Use current velocity, clearance, and actuator state to reject proposals that already fail a lower bound on transit time. Require that the total sensing-to-brake-onset travel plus braking distance fit inside the current clearance before granting motion. If no feasible fallback exists from this state, refuse the proposal. Refuse also when fresh evidence shows more than one candidate in the pick window, and route the item to the coworker for a manual pick. This stage admits a target and effort ceilings, never a path; admission of the whole trajectory belongs to the planner's record (@sec-planning-behavior-seam).
4. **Authority latch:** Store only the MCU-approved target, effort ceilings, expiry no later than the evidence deadline, and selected fallback. Arm the local timer for the admitted interval. The untrusted requested expiry and terminal mode do not control the drive directly.
5. **Runtime check:** On each configured control tick and relevant hardware fault event, compare measured state with the admitted limits. On evidence expiry, missed renewal, or an observed violation, revoke the proposal and start the previously validated response. The ensuing braking and hold have their own measured delay and physical margin.

When the Safety MCU latches an admitted proposal in Stage 4, it emits the certified contract record consumed by the trajectory planner (@tbl-10-intent-specification-contract).

\Needspace{26\baselineskip}

| Field                    | Representation                  | Physical semantics                                                                                                            | Invariant and consumer check                                                                          |
|:-------------------------|:--------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `magic` & `version`      | `uint32_t[2]`                   | Magic bytes (`0x494E5453`, 'INTS') and contract revision                                                                      | Statically reject mismatched schema revisions across inter-core boundary                              |
| `parent_belief_digest`   | `uint8_t[32]` (SHA-256)         | Digest of upstream Spatial Belief record (Contract 8)                                                                         | Establishes custody chain; matches retained belief record in memory                                   |
| `intent_digest`          | `uint8_t[32]` (SHA-256)         | Digest over all admitted fields in this record                                                                                | Emitted to Trajectory Record (Contract 10) to bind downstream planning                                |
| `evidence_epoch_ns`      | `uint64_t` (ns)                 | Physical measurement epoch $t_0$ from sensor transduction                                                                     | Evaluated on MCU clock; upper age must not exceed $\tau_{\text{ev}}$                                  |
| `admission_epoch_ns`     | `uint64_t` (ns)                 | Monotonic hardware timestamp when proposal was admitted                                                                       | Baseline epoch for administrative lease duration $\tau_{\text{lease}}$                                |
| `expiration_deadline_ns` | `uint64_t` (ns)                 | Absolute hardware deadline $t_{\text{exp}} = \min(t_0+\tau_{\text{ev}}, t_{\text{adm}}+\tau_{\text{lease}}, t_{\text{stop}})$ | Countdown timer revokes tracking authority upon expiry (@eq-intent-lease-expiry-bound)                |
| `frame_ids`              | `uint32_t[2]`                   | Base frame $\mathcal{F}_{\text{base}}$ and target affordance frame $\mathcal{F}_{\text{affordance}}$                          | Verified against active kinematic tree; prevents frame confusion                                      |
| `target_pose_se3`        | `double[7]`                     | Admitted nominal pose $[x, y, z, q_x, q_y, q_z, q_w]$ in $\mathcal{F}_{\text{base}}$                                          | Kinematically reachable within $\mathcal{W}$; swept-volume collision-free                             |
| `goal_region`            | `double[3]` (m), `double` (rad) | Spatial semi-axes $(r_x, r_y, r_z)$ and angular tolerance $\theta_{\text{tol}}$                                               | Defines $SE(3)$ goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ (@eq-intent-goal-set-se3); terminal boundary     |
| `dynamic_limits`         | `double[2]` (m/s, m/s²)         | Admitted TCP speed ceiling $v_{\max}$ and acceleration $a_{\max}$                                                             | Evaluated against thermal ratings; bounds transit lower bound (@eq-intent-dynamic-reachability-bound) |
| `max_wrench`             | `double[6]` (N, N·m)            | Admitted wrench ceiling $[F_x, F_y, F_z, \tau_x, \tau_y, \tau_z]$                                                             | Low-level impedance bounds; guards against crushing fragile items                                     |
| `validated_predicates`   | `uint32_t` (bitmask)            | Bitmask of verified predicates ($P_{\text{approach}}, P_{\text{contact}}, P_{\text{clear}}$)                                  | Planner must satisfy all asserted predicates across candidate trajectory                              |
| `fallback_policy_id`     | `uint32_t` (enum)               | Enforced terminal response (`HOLD`, `STOP`, `TORQUE_OFF`)                                                                     | MCU-selected deterministic safe state matched to measured load and contact                            |

: **Intent Specification contract record (Contract 9)**: Schema, data types, physical semantics, and invariant checks for the certified intent contract emitted by the Safety MCU and consumed by trajectory planning. {#tbl-10-intent-specification-contract tbl-colwidths="[20,18,32,30]"}

The **Intent Specification** contract record (@tbl-10-intent-specification-contract) acts as the formal contract boundary between spatial memory and trajectory planning. By anchoring `parent_belief_digest` to the upstream `SpatialBeliefRecord` (Contract 8, @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema) and emitting its own `intent_digest` to the downstream `TrajectoryRecord` (Contract 10, @sec-planning-behavior-seam), it creates an unbroken, auditable custody chain from raw camera photons to motor currents. Trajectory planners cannot alter the admitted geometric goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$ (@eq-intent-goal-set-se3), nor can they extend tracking beyond `expiration_deadline_ns`.

Filled in for the red mug, the lease admitted for the pick carries six entries. Its parent is the mug-handle belief record of @sec-memory-spatial-state-schema, matched by digest and evidence epoch. Its goal is the handle pose, and its error envelope is that record's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.e0_str` initial error, inside a `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.r_tol_str` task tolerance. Its evidence horizon is the age at which the governing growth law reaches that tolerance, `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str` under the record's belt-drift law and `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str` under the residual-slip law of the qualified tracker's renewed record. Its speed ceiling is the arm's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.v_tcp_str` tool-center-point speed limit, and it requests no item-specific wrench ceiling, because none is registered for the mug. The configured task and actuator ceilings still bound the wrench, and fragility is handled by the site's control of which items reach the conveyor, not by the controller. Its requested terminal mode is grasp, then hold for the handover, although the MCU still selects the fallback from its approved responses. Its expiry is the earliest of that evidence horizon, the configured lease ceiling, and the stop deadline.

This record gives @sec-verification a concrete interface for fault-injection tests in which corrupted quaternions, stale capture records, oversize force requests, and incompatible terminal requests should each be rejected under the tested state and timing conditions.

::: {#chk-intent-wire-schema-watchdogs .callout-checkpoint title="Expiring intent and fallback authority"}

Verify your understanding of how a proposal is refused or admitted, and how the lease granted from it is sized and revoked:

- [ ] **Ambiguity refusal**: Why must a pick window holding two candidates refuse the proposal, and why must that test run on a confident proposal as well as an uncertain one?
- [ ] **Wrong-object premise**: Which premise about the grasped object remains outside the permission path even when every coordinate, reachability, and force check passes, and where does the machine carry that premise instead?
- [ ] **Evidence horizon**: Can you explain why the evidence horizon of an intent lease is bounded by task tolerance and target drift rather than by the reasoning model's period, and why inflating it to hide tail inference latency leaves motion on an obsolete target?
- [ ] **Clock domain**: Why must the MCU convert the belief record's evidence epoch into its own monotonic clock, with a bounded conversion error, before checking age and the requested expiry?
- [ ] **Fallback selection**: Can you explain why the MCU must select a feasible approved hold, deceleration, or torque-disable response from the measured load state rather than obey the proposal's requested terminal mode?

:::

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-intent-fallacies-pitfalls}

Each mistake in this section trusts an upstream message to mean more than it does. Local checks\index{Local checks!authority withdrawal} must refuse a target, or withdraw tracking authority over one, when its evidence expires or its physical justification dissolves, and they must decide on evidence the proposer does not control, even while its messages remain well formed and confident.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *A renewal computed from the same stale frame is a valid renewal.*

The machine's intent model re-reads its last wrist-camera frame of the red mug and sends a renewal with a newer sequence number, a later issue time, and the same pose. Every field a keepalive would check has advanced, yet no image has been captured since the evidence that justified the target, and the mug has kept moving at `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.v_conveyor_str`. Because the lease dates its evidence by the belief record's evidence epoch\index{Lease!evidence epoch}, not by the renewal's issue time, the MCU matches the renewal's parent digest and epoch to the retained record, finds the epoch unchanged, and keeps counting age from the original capture. The target still expires `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str` after that capture. A controller that dated evidence by message arrival would let a stream of well-formed renewals hold an obsolete target indefinitely, turning the drift hazard of @sec-intent-goals-expire from a single late inference into a standing condition. **Advancing software timestamps on stale sensory data creates an illusion of liveliness while unobserved physical drift violates clearance.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Anchor lease validity strictly to the sensor evidence epoch $t_0$ of the parent belief record; reject renewals that fail to supply a certified newer hardware capture timestamp.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Allowing an unexpired temporal lease to continue commanding motion when target spatial bounds are violated.*

The machine's arm lowers its gripper toward the red mug under an intent with the `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.r_tol_str` grasp tolerance. A slip on the takeaway conveyor carries the mug beyond that tolerance while time still remains on the lease. The timestamp still permits execution, but the target has left the $SE(3)$\index{SE(3)!spatial bounds} region that justified the approach. Continuing until expiry would preserve an obsolete, potentially colliding command. The local perception and permission loops\index{Perception!local loop} must compare the observed target with the intent's spatial bounds and withdraw permission when those bounds fail\index{Lease!spatial invalidation}. Encoding that geometric condition in the lease allows the controller to interrupt the descent without waiting for a new high-level plan. **A temporal lease confers authority only within declared spatial bounds; temporal freshness never excuses spatial divergence.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Embed runtime spatial containment checks ($E(\Delta t) \le r_{\text{tol}}$) in high-rate control loops, instantly terminating motion authority if target drift or workpiece slip breaches tolerance mid-lease.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *A confident grounding needs no refusal path.*

A confidence score cannot certify that the scene holds only one candidate. A design that sends only low-confidence proposals to the ambiguity test treats the model's score as evidence about the scene, when it is the model's report about itself. The glass jar beside the red mug in @sec-intent-request-to-proposal arrives with a high score and a tight geometric envelope, so a score-gated design skips the test exactly where the test was needed. The refusal path\index{Refusal!confident grounding} must run on every proposal and must draw on evidence the model does not produce. A check that the pick window holds exactly one object refuses the jar-beside-mug scene whatever the score. What such a check cannot see, a lone jar arriving where the mug should be, remains a premise the permission path names rather than settles, and the site's feed procedure, which admits to the conveyor only items on the station's declared list, is what contains it. **Neural softmax confidence reflects internal model agreement, not real-world uniqueness; an ungrounded argmax over candidate clusters guarantees collision.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Mandate independent physical candidate counting in the task pick window; treat `ERR_GROUNDING_AMBIGUITY` as an admissible, first-class control outcome that routes execution to a safe hold or operator handoff.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Neural networks can resolve bimodal spatial ambiguity by averaging candidate target locations.*

In end-to-end imitation learning and behavioral cloning, training a deterministic neural policy with Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss mathematically forces the network to output the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}]$ under multimodal demonstrations. Faced with two equally valid candidate grasp targets, the network commands the spatial centroid between them, driving the end effector straight into empty air or colliding with intervening fixtures.

The machine sees two identical red mugs set a few centimeters apart on the takeaway conveyor and receives their spatial mean as a grasp target. The midpoint lies in empty space, so averaging has destroyed the $SE(3)$\index{SE(3)!target precision} distinction the task requires. Both mugs are real, so the innovation check of @sec-memory-belief-through-occlusion rejects neither measurement before fusion. Each hypothesis alone is sharp, and a gate applied to either one passes. The window check of @sec-intent-failure-modes still catches the case, because it counts two candidates in the pick window and the admission gate\index{Admission gate!rejection} refuses the proposal and maintains a hold, whatever the fused estimate reports. A covariance gate\index{Uncertainty!covariance expansion} would catch it only for an estimator that reports the bimodal ambiguity\index{Bimodal ambiguity!spatial}, which an averaging estimator does not. The intent interface must preserve statistical uncertainty rather than collapse competing object hypotheses into an apparently precise Cartesian coordinate, because only a representation that keeps both hypotheses lets a check other than the window count see the ambiguity. **Averaging bimodal physical targets replaces two valid manipulation candidates with a guaranteed crash into empty space.**

**Architect's countermeasure:** Preserve explicit multi-hypothesis distributions at the reasoning boundary (via diffusion policies or Gaussian mixture models), and enforce discrete candidate selection backed by the independent pick-window ambiguity gate.

:::

## Summary {#sec-intent-summary}

Grounded intent meets a request whose meaning the permission path cannot check, and it keeps the third law, that proposal is not permission, because the path grants only what it can check. A learned model proposes a dated target and an uncertainty description. The record the permission path grants from that proposal is the intent lease, which takes its evidence epoch and parent from the belief record of @sec-memory and grants a target and effort ceilings with an expiry no later than the evidence horizon that target drift and task tolerance set. An independent countdown then withdraws authority that a stalled model could never cancel. The independent permission path checks the target's evidence age, configured motion bounds, current state, path clearance, and feasible fallback before applying motion. The target-evidence horizon $\tau_{\text{ev}}\le(r_{\text{tol}}-e_0)/v_{\text{drift}}$ limits how long the target estimate may be used under its stated drift bound; it grants no time to stop, which a separate total-delay and braking check must find within the available physical clearance.

The red mug on the conveyor makes the cadence constraint concrete. Its untracked evidence lasts `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_untracked_str`, and the machine's `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.f_intent_str` intent model, refreshing every `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.t_intent_period_str`, cannot maintain that target by itself. A qualified local tracker can refresh it from new evidence and lengthen the horizon to `{python} IntentLeaseArchetypes.tau_tracked_str`, leaving the intent model only to re-confirm which mug is meant; otherwise the machine slows, pauses, or refuses the task. Expiry revokes the proposal's tracking authority and invokes a response validated for the measured state. It cannot undo motion already executed.

What grounded intent adds to the law is evidence age on a moving target, and refusal as the permission path's answer to what it can detect but not resolve. A target the arm cannot reach inside its evidence window fails the transit lower bound before any path is solved, a pick window holding two candidates fails the ambiguity test, and each rejection returns a reason the proposer can act on. The wrong-object case marks the limit of that machinery. A confident grounding to the wrong entity passes every geometric and timing check, so the premise that the grasped object is the named one stays open rather than being settled by the controller. After contact, a force trip bounds later loading only through the measured response, and precontact limits are what bound the first impact.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Grounded intent at the proposal boundary"}
* **A lease grants a target, never a path:** The Brain supplies a target, evidence epoch, error envelope, task tolerances, and requested expiry, and it writes no actuator setpoints. The permission path admits a target and effort ceilings that expire at the earliest of the evidence horizon, the lease ceiling, and the stop deadline.
* **The Intent Specification emits verified goal sets:** The 9th contract in the contract lineage binds admitted affordance frames, validated motion predicates, and geometric goal regions into an immutable record consumed by trajectory planners.
* **Evidence expires with drift:** Target drift and task tolerance set a finite validity horizon under a declared validity region. A fresh timestamp does not make a target correct, and only fresh evidence, never a faster model, renews it.
* **The evidence deadline is not the motion deadline:** The permission path separately budgets sensing, communication, enforcement, actuator delay, and braking distance for the current state and clearance.
* **Geometry cannot verify meaning:** A confident grounding to the wrong object can pass every coordinate, reachability, and force check. That premise needs its own task evidence, because the permission path cannot settle it.
* **Refusal is an admissible outcome:** Ambiguous identity, stale evidence, insufficient reachability, or infeasible stopping can each reject a proposal, and a structured rejection tells the proposer what to change. Each check has its own evidence limit.
:::

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From intent leases to trajectory planning"}
The Intent Specification (emitted at runtime as the admitted intent lease record) provides the formal spatial and temporal boundary conditions: the terminal $SE(3)$ goal set $\mathcal{G}_{\text{goal}}$, verified affordance frames, task tolerances, maximum wrench ceilings, and hard expiration deadline. @Sec-planning takes these certified constraints as input to synthesize the continuous, jerk-limited polynomial splines that execute within the admitted space-time tube. When an upcoming trajectory chunk is delayed in flight, the planner relies on the lease's pre-validated terminal state to guarantee a feasible stopping trajectory from every reachable state.
:::
